#4373. Starseed Asnia Trigger tier list and a reroll guide

This game features a lot of stunning, super-intelligent AI girls of Seven Themes, and we're going to rank them by power on this Starseed tier list.

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version: 6.20

In your fight against Redshift, you must command a team of beautiful AI girls. These girls are called Proxyans and are programmed to obey you at all times. Now, it’s on you to pick only the strongest for your team or else get decimated by Redshift and its minions.

But the thing is, there are 50+ Proxyans to choose from. There are attackers, defenders, and support units in the mix. When creating the ‘perfect’ team, you’ll need the best in every position. Now, if you were to test every Proxyan for yourself, it would take a lot of time and resources just to acquire each one.

But before that, know that there are other lists that you can use, like this Bump Superbrawl tier list, or our Sword of Convallaria tier list, for example. There are others too - just look around!

We’ve created a Starseed Asnia Trigger tier list that focuses on battlefield performance rather than the stats. Just click on the big blue button and get ready for a few surprises!

Original article by Shah Zaib. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

These two Proxyans are very different from each other. Rachel is a front-row attacker and Rayhou is a support/healer. Their skills are poles apart, but they have one thing in common: they're both overpowered!

It would be no surprise if the next major update nerfs these two a bit.

Yeah, the S tier is looking a little overpopulated, but that’s because there are plenty of ‘great’ characters in the game. Some of these Proxyans don’t look S-tier worthy in the Proxyans Data section, but boy, do they make up for it on the battlefield.

Other characters in this part of our Starseed tier list are all true to their stats. Claudia and Eradica are two of the best AoE Proxyans. Pick the one whose Passives suit your team the best. Freyja is a long-range attacker with solid debuffs up her sleeve, especially if you have plenty of Computators in your team.

If you are saving Recruit Tickets or thinking of performing a reroll, these are the units you want to target.

Chances are, most of you have already recruited these girls. And unless you get the S-tiers, you’ll have to make do with these. That’s not necessarily a bad thing. Pick the ones that suit your playstyle and invest heavily in them.

Take Yuna as an example. If you study her skills and use her right, she is one of the best single-target attackers in the game that also dishes out AoE damage with her Ultimate. The best thing about her is that she doesn’t need much help from her teammates either.

Similarly, Itus is a solid defender who can protect your precious attackers and healers while doing decent AoE damage. But, you’ll have to spend a lot of Credits and Tactical Manuals to bring her up to par.

If you have any of these characters, equip them with the right gear and do proper Optimization. Then, and only then, some of these can give the S-tier characters a run for their money.

Welcome to the tier of all-show-no-go Proxyans. These girls have flashy skills that look cool but don’t do much on the battlefield.

If you get some of these Proxyans, keep them around for specific missions and team builds. However, spending too many resources on these characters is wasteful.

These are the most disappointing Proxyans in the game because their skills and stats look good, but it doesn’t translate to performance, hence they fall down to tier C. But they are still better than the near-useless characters that have ended up in the D tier.

By now, you probably have an idea of which characters to roll for or go through the trouble of rerolling for. In case you jumped straight to our reroll guide, check out the S tier, as those are the characters to chase if you want to crush your enemies. And A-tier characters are there for those who like a challenge.

Now, let’s discuss how to reroll in Starseed Asnia Trigger. Even if you have already linked an account, you can still delete it and start over. Things will be a bit easier for those who started out with a guest account, though.

To perform a reroll, follow these steps: Tap on the three-line icon in the top-right corner of your main screen and open Settings. Tap on the Account tab. Click on the Tap to Go Now button next to the Delete Account option.

Once you confirm account deletion, the game will reload and ask you to select an account to sync with. This is where you want to sign in as a guest. This will make things easier in case you don’t get the desired character and have to perform another reroll.

Now, simply skip the introductory video, or play through it if you’d like to enjoy the not-so-subtle fan service.

As Starseed Asnia Trigger walks you through your first fight that can not be skipped or put on auto mode, it’ll take you up to five minutes to finally get into the game. Skip past a few more tutorials and win FOUR battles to unlock the Recruit feature.

From there on, it’s all about luck. If you get your desired Proxyan, simply link an account or be ready to spend another 10-15 minutes doing everything all over again. Once you're happy with your lot, redeem these Starseed codes for a handy boost!

#4372. Zenless Zone Zero's new Krampus squad know when you've been bad or good in a Christmas-y update to close out 2025

Zenless Zone Zero's 2.4 update is a chunky one, adding a new faction to the action RPG's roster alongside a new area, and fresh playable characters.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program was a big one, bringing us all the news about Version 2.4, the next major update. It’s called On the Precipice of the Abyss, and it will be available to download on November 26.

On the Precipice of the Abyss has tendrils in many areas of the game, touching several parts of its fiction as well as gameplay, so it’s one to watch out for.

Version 2.4’s biggest claim to fame is the introduction of the Krampus Compliance Authority, a new faction that’s affiliated with TOPS. This looks to be the oversight committee, dispatched after the squad’s adventure beneath Timesworn Hill.

The events of this narrative arch follow on from the Timesworn Hill crisis, which is partly why we’re going to a new area as part of this update. The old mining site can now be explored for the first time in a decade, now that the Miasma has begun to recede.

Our newcomers this time around are Dialyn and Banyue. Dialyn is an S-Rank Physical Stun Agent who’s a former customer service specialist. This isn’t just a backstory, however, as it plays into her gameplay.

Dialyn relies on two resources: Customer Complaint and Positive Review, but her core role is to stun enemies and allow teammates to unleash their Ults, with a nice boost to boot.

Banyue is another S-Rank, though he’s a Fire Rupture Agent. He uses his martial arts expertise to create combinations of might and grandeur. In combat, he pulls from Adrenaline and Wrathful Fires, alternating between the two to fuel his actions. There’s a bit of rhythm to his gameplay that might take you a little while to master.

Even more characters will join as part of this update, in the form of not one but two new Bangboo units. Birkblick is Krampus' own proprietary lil bunny fella, who brings a sensor array that can transform into a cannon in combat, essentially tracking and immediately nuking targets. Then there’s Bild N. Boolok, a Support Agent-affiliated Physical damage dealing Bangboo bringing a giant block hammer to the fight to, well, smash enemies with.

It’s a bit of a winter party in Version 2.4, it seems, as the update will bring back Hugo (Attack - Ice), and Ellen (Attack - Ice), too.

You can also look forward to the return of the Bangboo auto chess event, which now includes PvE stages with unique rewards. In fact, playing this event is how you could get Bild N. Boolok for free. Lightstream Notes is another event that will be available for the duration of this update, and it will let you tag along with Ye Shunguang to New Eridu.

#4371. Every WoW Forever Class Ranked For Leveling

Jake brings two decades of experience covering video games, MTG, covering industry events on-site, delivering breaking news and major interviews.

We made it. World of Warcraft: Forever is finally here.

November 4th brings the long-awaited debut of “Classic Plus” in World of Warcraft, which means it’s time to start the journey anew. Again. We’re starting as a lowly, nameless level 1 character in Azeroth. Sure, we can see Blackrock Mountain and Hyjal in the distance from the starting areas, but we’re a long, long way from getting there.

The leveling process from 1-60 in Classic lasts a lot longer than it does in retail WoW. Even the most efficient players will take 150-200 hours to level in-game. It could take weeks, if not months, for players to hit max level. Not that this is a bad thing; Classic WoW is about the journey, not the destination.

With that being said, the journey in World of Warcraft can look different for everyone, depending not just on your time and ability, but on your class as well. You know what that means: it’s time for a tier list. Let’s go over every WoW: Forever class ranked for leveling.

When it comes to classic World of Warcraft, there was always one certainty: Warriors ruled the endgame.

With that being said, they had to earn it, as their leveling experience was, in a word, frustrating. Sure, they can tank through dungeons, but the issue is that the class does not thrive in solo-oriented content, which is what leveling generally is.

Thanks to dungeon XP nerfs outside quests, dungeon grinding isn't really on the table, though you do have some improvements available. Still, it's going to be a slow and tedious process to level up your Warrior.

The good news is that Rogues are doing excellent single-target damage (highest in the game, according to Blizzard), along with an impressive toolkit to be beneficial. The bad news is that all of the shortcomings that come with the Classic Rogue are still here.

That's not to say it's "bad," per se, but you can make the argument that outside of that single-target damage, it's outclassed by almost every other class.

The newest beta build for World of Warcraft: Forever has included some pretty controversial changes, including dungeon quest XP and class changes.

The biggest "issue" Priests have is that they're easily the worst DPS caster during the leveling process. That said, they can, you know, heal and bring along the utility that comes with a healer.

Like Rogues, they suffer from being outclassed by other, better options, but have the benefit of being a healer to help with survivability. Even in their post-nerf form, your wands are still extremely powerful.

You'll also never be unable to find a group...provided you're willing to heal, that is. Shadow can at least let you properly DPS while leveling alone, but it's nowhere near as powerful as the other caster classes.

Druids take a while to get going, but when they do, you'll be in for an enjoyable time. You just have to, you know, get there.

On the plus side, Druid lets you play any role you want: Tank, Healer, Melee DPS, Ranged DPS, hating life from levels 1-10. You name it, Druids can do it.

I'm being serious on that last one, sadly; the initial leveling experience is frustrating, and while it finally starts to get better as you access talents, it's still a slog to get through. On the plus side, you can get into any dungeon you want by being able to play any role needed.

If you believed everything you read on the internet, especially when it comes to World of Warcraft discourse, you'd feel like Shamans are far and away the worst class in the game. We're not here to talk about that, though. We're here to talk about how classes feel during the leveling process, and Shamans are solid.

Enhancement Shamans will be able to dish out plenty of damage while still tapping into the usefulness and resources available in the class toolkit, particularly healing, to make it one of the best melee leveling classes in the game outside of Paladins. Leveling as Elemental, though, still feels quite bad, so I recommend you avoid that spec as long as possible.

Will WoW: Forever be worth the time when it releases? Check out DualShockers impressions.

We're a long way away from the 2019 version of Mage leveling, as AOE farming in the open world has been nerfed. That said, Mages are still mages, so they have that going for them.

Mages can dish out damage, good AOE damage (especially at low levels), good crowd control, and the ability to always have immediate access to food and drinks. They remain efficient at the leveling process in World of Warcraft: Forever, but they're not as strong as they once were.

First of all, Undead Paladins are here in WoW: Forever, and I am beyond excited for it. They were the first class I tried in beta, and oh my goodness, it felt fantastic.

Obviously, some balance changes have gone live since then, but the class feels like it's in fantastic shape. Playing a Paladin is fun, the quality-of-life changes are nice, and it feels like you can take on the world even at lower levels. It's one of the strongest classes to level in WoW: Forever, only outclassed by a select few options.

RP PVP servers are back on the menu for World of Warcraft: Forever!

I'll talk about Hunters later on in this list, since, spoiler alert, they're still the best class for leveling in WoW Forever, but there are a lot of similar features to a Warlock. Your pets will do a lot of damage and hold aggro, letting you safely cast spells from a distance.

The one difference between Warlocks and Hunters, though, is that Hunters do more damage and have less downtime. Still, Warlocks have impressive utility and never, ever die (or at least they never, ever should).

Hunters have always been leveling gods throughout the Classic WoW timeline for one reason: the strength of their pet.

Until Jokerd came along on his mage in 2019 with constant AOE farming, Hunters, notably Joana, always held the world record for 1-60 leveling for one simple reason: little to no downtime.

Your pet can tank enemies while dishing out legitimate damage as you, the player, attack safely from a range while constantly moving forward. Hunters rock as levelers, and Forever cements them as still the undisputed best leveling class in World of Warcraft.

Classic Plus is real! It's finally coming!

#4369. Battlefield 6 gets a new map today alongside major changes to controller aim assist, and even more weapon dispersion tweaks

Right on schedule, the latest Battlefield 6 patch has arrived to kick off the next stage of Season 1.

Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major update earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The update, of course, also adds new content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

We’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The update kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a new limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other big new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

These are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Redsec players have a new Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

The fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a big overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several issues that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version 2.1.0 - Latest Additions: Arianaute, Shelirionach Wizardry Variants Daphne is not one of those gacha RPGs many of us are accustomed to. Instead, it follows a more classical approach to the genre, and I personally couldn't be happier to play something like this. So much so, I made a complete Wizardry Variants Daphne tier list of all the characters you can recruit. So, if you want to know who you should have on your team, this is where you can find all the info you need.

I'll start off by saying that this is giving me insane Final Fantasy VIII vibes - the visuals, the interactions, everything. I know that you could make a lot of the heroes work if you just upgrade them enough and equip them with the proper gear, but if you really want to maximise your potential, our Wizardry Variants Daphne codes will also prove useful.

About the Wizardry Variants Daphne tier list Below, you will find all the characters with their original name ranked according to how well they perform right now. Keep in mind the list is based on the Global version, so any upcoming characters are not ranked until they've been released and I've tested them in battle.

I've ranked the best characters in the S+ tier, so when you are just getting started and have to select one guaranteed Legendary, make sure you pick one of the best-ranking options. I've added them to the reroll tier list on the last page, too, so make sure to consult that if you want to min-max.

Our complete Wizardry Variants Daphne tier list is on the following pages, so either go with the quick links below or consult the entire list. whichever is more convenient for you! S+ tier  |  S tier  |  A tier  |  B tier  |  C tier  |  Reroll guide Original article by Cristina Mesesan. Updated by Mihail Katsoris.

Alice is a really amazing character to have from the start. She has a buff that increases damage dealt to enemies if she only has neutral or evil allies, so you always need to consider that when making your team. She is currently the best Priest. Lanavaille and Wanderer Princess Lanavaille are two different versions (Wanderer Princess is another style for Lanavaille), and they are both exceptional. I slightly prefer Wanderer Princess Lanavaille since she boosts her own Action Speed based on the gear she has, but overall, both versions constantly increase her stats with the Discipline skill, while with her Inherit skill, she can also heal allies when winning a battle.

Yekaterina is pretty good in terms of damage, just like Adam, since they are both Mages. The difference is that Yekaterina can basically disable ambushes on you, which is really helpful both at the start and during end-game battles. You just need to be mindful of where you place her. As for Adam, I have only tested him for a little while, and he goes well with Alice and a team of other Mages with lower MP cost. You can make him work in a few teams, actually, but I wouldn't recommend getting him as your first Legendary character (hence, he's only in the S-tier). Gerard is similar to Gerulf in terms of skills, but the difference is that he needs a one-handed sword, and he boosts his own Evasion instead of Accuracy. Similarly, he is decent, and with his Inherit skill, he has a slight chance to Paralyze enemies, but I wouldn't rely on that. Debra is outstanding. She can pair really well with Alice (since she is neutral), and she is able to scale really well into the late game, and also during battles - she can sustain her SP cost fairly well, so I recommend getting and using her if possible.

I managed to get Gerulf as well, and he is a pretty good Fighter to place on the front line. I like the fact that he uses a two-handed weapon, and his skill boosts his accuracy while he is equipped with one. He is not outstanding, but he is a decent team member if you want to go for an Evil/Neutral team. Mage of the Silent Night Flut has a really nice design in my opinion, and even though she is a Mage, she can be quite decent thanks to her skill scaling. I wouldn't rely on her as the sole source of damage, though.

Elf-Mag is the only Anonymous character that is worth upgrading in my opinion, since she has decent stats. I wouldn't recommend going ham and rerolling for her, though, since you'll get her eventually. Gandolfo and Jean are also decent, but I wouldn't bother investing too much time and resources into them. Just use them until you can get something better, because the more you advance, the less they'll be able to keep up. At least, that's how it was for me.

All the characters at the bottom of our Wizardry Variants Daphne tier list can be used at the start of the game, but I wouldn't bother upgrading any of them further or taking them into battle. I've tried and tested Eldorado, Gastol, and Elda, but I was not very happy with the results, so I strongly suggest you only use them until you get something better.

You will get a lot of bones at the beginning, so just try to summon something you will actually need. On the next page, you will find a reroll guide so you can start over if things don't go according to plan on the first try!

To reroll in Wizardry Variants Daphne is a little bit time-consuming, but it can be done nonetheless. How long does one reroll take? To complete one reroll (and I mean start over and go through the process ONCE), you will need about 20-30 minutes. Depending on how quickly you move and know what to do, it can be roughly 20 minutes. Otherwise, more like 25-30 minutes. It is not quick, but if you're determined to go all out and start with the best possible characters, go for it. How to reroll in Wizardry Variants Daphne (step by step) This is how you reroll in Wiz Daphne:

Step 1: Play through the tutorial, up to the point where you are asked the 10 questions to determine your personality. The best personality you can get is Neutral, so the main character can benefit from more buffs.Step 2: Continue playing until you reach the town alongside Lulu, and then go to Adventurer's Guild and accept the quest to rescue the King.Step 3: Open the Guild Mailbox and take all the rewards you have there so you can summon for free. If you want, you can also exchange all the Gems for bones at the Jeweler (Jeweler> Limited Time Offer). Step 4: Go to Ruins and select Right Hand of Reversal.Step 5: Summon, and try to obtain one of the best-ranked characters in the game. If you are happy with the summons you get, then continue playing the game. Head over to the Abyss, then back to town, and you will encounter a bone picker NPC. He will give you a choice of one free Legendary character. If you are not happy, proceed to the next step!Step 6: Close the game and re-open it. Do not tap on Start, instead go to Settings> Delete User Data. That will delete all your progress, and you can start over from Step 1. #4367. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Review - Still In Motion

Originating as a tech demo for the Wii’s motion controls, Nintendo’s Sports series has always found novel and intuitive ways to emulate various athletic endeavors with motion-based video game controllers. Like its predecessors, Switch Sports Resort is a compilation of sports-based minigames built around approachability. Though rightfully known for its enticing multiplayer options, Switch Sports Resort adds new single-player objectives and modes to offer a well-rounded experience for all player counts, making it perhaps the strongest entry in the series to date.

Switch Sports Resort delivers 12 main events to choose from, each with distinct controls, strategies, and rules. Mainstays like bowling, archery, boxing, and golf were my initial destinations to attempt to relive old glories, but newcomers like thumb wrestling, skateboarding, power cruising, and prop plane made me glad for their inclusion.

Skateboarding, power cruising, and prop plane form a new category called leisure sports, which allow for timed exploration of the newly renovated Wuhu Island by land, sea, and sky, respectively. I spent several sessions seeking out landmarks and collecting Spocco Points, the in-game currency used for character customization. And since all the sports’ controls are so intuitive and newcomer-friendly, it was a breeze to jump between activities.

Though they all boil down to moving your arms in something approximating motions you’d make playing the real sport, Nintendo has smartly implemented more variety in its control schemes, all while keeping them easy to pick up. Before the tutorial even explains how to hold the Joy-Con, you can likely accurately guess what the grip and motion will be; even more involved control schemes like basketball and volleyball are easy to remember.

Skateboarding is particularly innovative, as it uses Switch 2’s Joy-Con’s mouse mode to emulate the kick-push of a skater. Meanwhile, prop plane has you holding your Joy-Con like a paper airplane as you fly around blasting balloons and visiting landmarks. However, holding the Joy-Con that way for several minutes inevitably cramped my hand. And though boxing remains one of my favorite sports in the bundle, I needed to retrain my brain, as throwing a punch the correct way doesn’t work with how the game wants you to do it; if I turn my wrist when punching, my character sways instead of attacking.

Playing with friends, both online and in-person, remains the highlight of Switch Sports Resort. The online friend lobby system receives a boost in the form of allowing different sports to take place simultaneously within the same lobby, and when you add in special variants like simultaneous archery, 100-pin bowling, skateboard racing, and prop plane balloon battles, you have a lot of fun options with which to jump in.

Whenever I play solo, the Island Crown is where I spend most of my time. Here, you climb the ranks across nine sports, sometimes with special rulesets, vanquishing NPC opponents until you are the champion. Whether it was taking to increasingly outlandish bowling lanes, windier archery ranges, or simply facing off against more strategic table tennis players, I relished in improving my skills en route to the championship.

Because these minigames are relatively surface level, they have diminishing returns once you reach a certain skill level. While I loved it when my tennis opponents started challenging me to use better angles and my fellow golfers stopped air-mailing their tee shots straight into the trees, higher-skill opponents rarely energized me; instead, sports like bowling that include fun, off-the-wall variants were my favorite ladders to ascend, as they truly put my skills to the test as I was forced to adapt to moving obstacles and ramps. I just wish Nintendo injected more fun twists to keep the experiences fresh.

After completing each activity, you’re awarded Spocco Points, which you use to unlock themed customization elements for your characters. Cartoon-like Sportsmates replace the iconic Mii characters introduced in Wii Sports, but you can still use your Mii if you choose. Though I have fondness for Mii characters, after two entries featuring the more expressive, customizable Sportsmates, I now prefer those character models.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort delivers a capable compilation of quick-hit sports minigames that can be easily enjoyed regardless of how many people are holding Joy-Cons. Though I certainly have my destination sports, there’s not a loser in the bunch. Island Crown mode does a great job expanding the single-player options, but this package’s legs are in its multiplayer experience. And since Switch Sports Resort is chock-full of easily approachable minigames, I can see it becoming a cherished inclusion in the rotation of party mainstays.

#4366. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with... a questionable selection of maps, but at least the modes are good

If Redsec got you hooked on Battlefield gameplay but you never experienced traditional multiplayer in Battlefield 6, there's an upcoming moment you might want to pay attention to.

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

This is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

The Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

Instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two new maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

As for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

Beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two new maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

The miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for new players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

#4365. NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone

Nearly 50 years after leaving Earth, NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone that will highlight just how far humanity's most distant spacecraft has traveled. But keeping the aging explorer operational has become an increasingly difficult challenge as its power supply slowly fades.

NASA engineers recently achieved two important developments in their effort to extend the mission. In September, they completed a complex energy conservation project designed to preserve the spacecraft's remaining scientific capabilities. Then, on October 20, Voyager 1 unexpectedly resumed communication with Earth after a mysterious 48-hour interruption.

NASA Engineers Find a Clever Way to Save Power

In early September, the Voyager team successfully replaced three devices aboard Voyager 1 with alternatives that consume less electricity. The carefully coordinated operation, nicknamed the "Big Bang," took months to prepare and was completed approximately six weeks after engineers carried out an identical procedure on Voyager 2.

The upgrade is expected to extend the operating lives of Voyager 1's remaining scientific instruments, allowing the spacecraft to continue collecting valuable information from interstellar space longer than previously expected.

Both Voyager spacecraft generate electricity using radioisotope thermoelectric generators. These systems produce electrical power from the heat released as plutonium undergoes radioactive decay. As that process continues, the spacecraft gradually lose generating capacity, with each probe experiencing a decline of approximately 4 watts annually.

After almost five decades in space, that steady loss has left engineers with very little power to spare. To keep the missions operating, NASA has progressively shut down equipment that is no longer essential.

The Big Bang presented an especially difficult engineering challenge because all three replacements had to happen simultaneously. The six devices involved help maintain temperatures inside the spacecraft despite the extreme cold of space. Replacing the three original devices together was necessary to reduce electricity consumption while preserving the proper distribution of heat throughout Voyager 1.

Keeping Voyager 1's Science Mission Alive

Power limitations have already forced NASA to deactivate two of Voyager 1's scientific instruments in recent years. When the spacecraft launched in 1977, it carried 10 instruments dedicated to scientific research. Several were shut down after Voyager completed its encounters with the outer planets, while others remained active to investigate increasingly distant regions of space.

Among the areas studied was the outer heliosphere, the enormous region of particles and magnetic fields produced by the Sun. Both Voyager spacecraft have since crossed beyond this boundary into interstellar space, making them the only spacecraft ever to directly examine the environment outside the Sun's heliosphere.

Preserving their remaining instruments is particularly important because no other missions can currently collect measurements from this distant region. Without the Big Bang upgrade, NASA would have faced the possibility of shutting down another Voyager 1 instrument as early as summer 2027.

Mysterious Communication Loss Raises New Questions

Even with the successful power conservation effort, Voyager 1 continues to encounter unexpected problems.

NASA temporarily lost contact with the spacecraft on October 18 and 19, when the agency's Deep Space Network failed to receive its radio signal during two scheduled communication attempts separated by 24 hours.

The network consists of large radio antennas at three locations around the world, allowing NASA to exchange signals with spacecraft exploring the Moon and more distant destinations. At the time of the interruption, Voyager 1 was approximately 16 billion miles (24 billion kilometers) from Earth.

After two unsuccessful attempts to detect the spacecraft, its signal unexpectedly returned on October 20, roughly 48 hours after the interruption began. Communication has remained established since then, and engineers subsequently sent commands to investigate the problem.

NASA has not yet determined exactly what caused the incident. However, engineers discovered that one set of Voyager 1's thrusters had stopped operating and that the spacecraft had automatically activated its backup thrusters.

This behavior is part of a built-in safety system known as fault protection. When the onboard computers recognize a potential problem with active equipment, they can switch to backup hardware, place the spacecraft into a stable configuration, and suspend normal activities. This gives controllers on Earth an opportunity to investigate and determine the appropriate response.

"This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," said Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "We're relieved to be back in contact with Voyager 1 and are eager to understand what happened."

Voyager 1 Approaches a Historic One-Light-Day Milestone

While NASA continues investigating the communication interruption, Voyager 1 is moving toward another remarkable achievement.

Traveling through interstellar space at approximately 38,000 mph (61,155 kph), the spacecraft is expected to reach a distance of 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth on November 18. That distance equals one light-day, meaning it takes light an entire 24 hours to travel between Earth and the probe.

No other human-made object has ever reached such a distance.

The milestone also illustrates the extraordinary challenges of communicating with a spacecraft so far from home. Radio waves travel at the speed of light, so commands transmitted from Earth will require a full day to reach Voyager 1. Any response sent back will take another 24 hours, creating a total communication delay of 48 hours.

"If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL.

Crossing the one-light-day threshold will not produce any physical change in Voyager 1 or its surroundings. The spacecraft will continue traveling through the same interstellar environment, unaware that it has passed a milestone of special significance to people on Earth.

Instead, the achievement serves as a powerful reminder of the enormous distances separating objects in the universe and the remarkable endurance of a spacecraft launched nearly half a century ago. Despite fading power, aging equipment, and unexpected technical problems, Voyager 1 continues its historic journey farther from Earth than any other human-made object.

Materials provided by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4363. Battlefield 6 streamlines some of the most annoying Challenges yet again, takes out a few of them entirely

The easier and more accessible Battlefield Studios makes those Battlefield 6 Challenges, the better.

The work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

The Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

The journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The issue encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing new Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently announced that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

#4362. Final Fantasy Resonance Review - On Its Own Wavelength

RPG publisher Square Enix has been doing the Lord's work lately by rescuing their discontinued mobile games and rehydrating them into full-fat RPG experiences. Last year's Octopath Traveler 0 is one such triumph, and it's safe to say Final Fantasy Resonance is another victory for reusing assets instead of throwing them in the garbage. More importantly, it's a great RPG experience with a fun cast and character customization options that will make fans of the Final Fantasy V job system rabid with delight.

Resonance is based on the first season of the now-defunct Final Fantasy Brave Exvius mobile game, which ran four chapters in total from 2016 to 2025, but Resonance is no mere port. For starters, it received an HD-2D injection that gussied up Exvius's already-impressive sprites. Resonance wears the HD-2D aesthetic confidently; Square Enix has obviously listened to past criticisms of its beloved graphical style, and it paid off. Resonance is an HD-2D game, but its highly detailed character sprites and occasional jaw-dropping pixel-based "cinema" scene differentiate it from the Octopath Traveler series and the Dragon Quest HD-2D remakes.

Resonance's distinctions are its greatest strength, in fact. It's easy to assume at first blush that its story about a boy and his best friend is nothing but a table to prop retro Final Fantasy references upon. It's true that a key part of Resonance's gameplay involves summoning "Visions" into battle, said visions being projections of characters from other Final Fantasy games. But that's all they are: Projections. They teach transferable skills, à la Final Fantasy V's job system. They can offer characters permanent stat boosts as they level up, like Final Fantasy VI's espers. And when conditions are met, they can be summoned to perform a super attack via a CGI spectacle that will remind you Square Enix have been masters of game cinema direction since day one.

Each Resonance character can equip a Vision that lends them their powers in a fight, and also grants passive upgrades and skills. Rain, for example, is a heavy hitter with innate fire attacks, but if he wears Cecil Harvey as a backpack, he also gets access to light and dark magic. Cecil gets stronger as they fight together, and bestows skills that can be equipped as wanted. If you're a Final Fantasy V job-head, you've come home.

But Final Fantasy Resonance is Rain's story despite its many callbacks to past games. Yes, Rain is an amalgamation of past Final Fantasy heroes, from Cloud's spiky yellow hair to Tidus's daddy issues, to Zidane's sunny attitude (with a hint of shadow), but that just makes him easier to root for. Rain's roommate, Lasswell, contains notes of my beloved Kain Highwind from Final Fantasy IV, but there's a troubled nobility to him that's purely his own. They're gradually joined by a cast of characters who click with each other (and thus, with me) thanks in part to comedic side-discussions delivered with quality voice acting. References to past Final Fantasy games are doled with clever subtlety. As a Final Fantasy XIV fan, I had to peel myself off the ceiling more than once when I encountered some choice shoutouts.

Resonance's battle system grants it another distinction. It's a classic turn-based system that shows off who's next in line to attack, like Final Fantasy X. Every character brings a fighting style and elemental flavor to the party. Lasswell is a samurai who favors ice, Jake is a gunner attuned to the wind, and Lid will rain the fattest of steel chocobos upon your head in an earth-based attack.

Resonance is a snappy game, which might be its most welcome trait. Fast travel is generous, and dungeons are conquered in just the right amount of time. You're looking at a 40-hour experience, give or take, which is downright digestible for an RPG in this day and age. On the flipside, Rain's world lacks depth. Its towns are beautiful, unique, and filled with characters and quest-givers who are worth talking to, but the overworld connective tissue is thin and its dungeons lack pizzazz. An auto-battle option would lessen the frustration of random encounters, but said encounters don't pop up nearly as often as they do in ancestral Final Fantasy games. Plus, the random battles are spaced in a way that makes grinding unnecessary unless you're maxing out a Vision, which I appreciate, but sometimes you're just trying to get to a place.

I went into Resonance expecting to like it for its salute to Final Fantasy characters across the decades, but I wound up loving the game for showing me a whole new canon. In a time when mainline Final Fantasy is still figuring itself out, Final Fantasy Resonance is easy to recommend. It has one foot planted on the solid foundation of Final Fantasy's history, but with its rich graphics and likeable cast of characters it builds up from that history instead of merely pillaging it.

It’s the same fuzzy feeling a lot of really high-quality mods give off, another for-fun creation format being plagued by more and more AI slop. Many would rather just not engage with this side of the space, and refusing to let them know before diving in is a hiccup I don’t think many studios will make after this debacle.

VR Chat is a corner of the gaming creative space I would hate to see falter, and I don’t think VR Chat Inc. is going to sit on this amount of community backlash. #4359. Arc Raiders patch nerfs the Deadline mine, ends the menace of the Venator

The first post-Stella Montis patch for Arc Raiders has arrived, and it predictably touches much of what people brought to the latest map.

Arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the new “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

#4358. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

After the greatest female pilot goes missing, players control a headache-suffering detective searching for her whereabouts. Zero Parades: For Dead Spies, the spiritual follow-up to Disco Elysium, only launched in May, but it already has a much-improved Director's Cut coming next month. This version features new scenes adding over 40,000 words), a backstage mode, a new dramatic encounter, voice-over improvements, new clothing items, a new death screen, inventory filtering, and more. #4355. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4354. Evo Brazil 2027 confirms eight-game lineup and R$1m prize pool as ticket sales open

Tobias Wren has been poking around the business side of competitive gaming for longer than most people have considered it a legitimate industry. He got hooked watching early LCS seasons and quickly realized the drama off the stage was just as interesting as anything happening on it. These days he spends most of his time tracking team valuations, sponsorship trends, and the broader money moves that shape where esports is actually headed.

Evo has set out the full plan for its first event in South America. Evo Brazil 2027 will run from 26 to 28 March 2027 at Expo Center Norte in São Paulo, with eight titles on the main lineup and at least R$1m in guaranteed prize money spread across those competitions.

Competitor registration and ticket sales both opened on Tuesday 27 October. Each tournament entry costs R$50 per game, while the first batch of spectator passes is priced at R$180 for a single day or R$490 for all three days, according to the official Evo Brazil website. That early tier is on sale until 28 December, after which regular and final batches push the full price up to R$250 and R$690 respectively.

In alphabetical order, the lineup is Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game, FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves, Guilty Gear -Strive-, MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls, Mortal Kombat 1, Street Fighter 6, TEKKEN 8 and THE KING OF FIGHTERS XV. All main events use open brackets, so any registered player can enter.

How the R$1m will be split between the eight titles has not yet been published. Alongside the main stage, the festival programme includes an Evo Museum, an Artist Alley, cosplay activities, an arcade area and space for community run side tournaments.

Launch day did not go entirely to plan. A few hours after the announcement, the official Evo Brazil account told fans that ticket sales had been paused. Sales resumed later that evening, with Evo explaining that it had fixed an internal technical error affecting the ticket prices shown on the site. Buyers who purchased before the correction will receive a partial refund covering the price difference.

São Paulo is one of several new stops planned under owner RTS, which is also taking the brand to China, Mexico, Morocco, Saudi Arabia and Singapore, on top of its established events in the US, Japan and France. The Esports Radar reports that the Latin American rollout is headed by Rafael Queiroz, Evo’s Head of LATAM and previously General Manager of Team Liquid Brazil.

Commercial backing for the debut comes from global partners Visa and PlayStation Tournaments. Visa signed on with Evo earlier this year in a deal that, per Evo’s own announcement, runs through early 2028.

Brazil is not new territory for the brand. São Paulo staged the Versus: Evo South America events in both 2008 and 2009, and Evo General Manager Rick Thiher pointed to that history in the press release: “Bringing Evo to São Paulo will be an opportunity to honour this legacy, highlight the incredible passion of Brazilian players and fans, and invite the global fighting game community to take part in the next chapter of Evo’s history.”

The March date also places Evo Brazil early in a busy 2027 competitive calendar, as publishers and organisers rework their circuits. Esports Insider recently looked at the new qualification routes for the Esports World Cup 2027.
