The GT-R (R35) Premium looks like a pretty good vehicle for this tier. Not only is it affordable, but it has an amazing grip (too much, perhaps?!) and a low shift time. You'll need to work on power and lowering the weight with a lighter body.

The Viper ACR is another good option: it has great power for the tier, a low shift time, and 23 Fusion Slots.

Right now, the Rocket Bunny is looking more attractive than ever, but the big Grand Cherokee Trackhawk is tempting too.

At this point, the game has some amazing cars to use, and the latest releases push performance to the limits. These are by far the fastest cars in CSR Racing 2. The Bugatti Chiron is a fantastic choice, as is the FXX K, but launch cars such as the Bugatti Veyron and One:1 are still great.

If you don't want to rely on Rare Import lot wins, the Aventador LP 700-4 is a good bet with its high power, strong grip, and its relatively lightweight to boot.

Regardless, though, there's no doubt you'll have fun with vehicles like the 'Cuda "TorC" in CSR2.

#4335. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Update 1.1 Adds Quality Of Life Improvements, Boosts Performance, and Adds Pettable Animals

We've been enjoying The Blood of Dawnwalker, one of the year's biggest games, but its release was a little rough around the edges. It took a lot of feedback from fans for developer Rebel Wolves to prioritize higher framerates at launch for consoles, but even then, the game certainly struggled at times on my PlayStation 5. Today, the game's first major update drops, and it aims to smooth some of those performance issues and introduce a few quality-of-life features.

The trailer above highlights combat-specific improvements, like improved targeting and animations, and a less restrictive camera. Rebel Wolves is also lowering the health of wolves and boars, who previously remained tanky even into the later hours of the game, and it should be easier to disengage from combat, should you choose to do so. For casual players, there's a new difficulty mode; what was previously "Story" mode has been renamed "Forgiving," while the new version of "Story" mode adds additional combat assists.

Rebel Wolves has also added some new features outside of combat. A new Daught of Mind Rebirth potion allows you to respec your skill tree, re-allocating time and skill points spent to switch up your build. You can also increase the size of subtitles (an option I'm always grateful for) and pet dogs and cats. Finally, the Shadowstep and Planeshift systems should be more responsive now – here's hoping I have an easier time teleporting onto rooftops instead of the wall right below them.

Those are the major, most visible highlights, but players can view the full patch notes here to see the hundreds of other minor improvements that aim to squash bugs, reduce crashes, and improve stability.

For more on The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can check out our review, in which our reviewer admires the swings the developers took, even though they don't always pay off. You can also check out our coverage hub for our issue devoted to The Blood of Dawnwalker, including interviews with its ex-Witcher development team.

#4334. Honkai: Star Rail 3.8 will run for an extra two weeks while Version 4.0 is in the oven

The next Honkai: Star Rail update is upon us, and there's a mix of good - and unusual news.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

This final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

It's been rebuilt to support touch controls and vertical play, and it will be available on iOS and Android. You can even play the first half of the game for free – the first four episodes are included, but you'll need to pay $19.99 to play the rest.

Shopify Rebellion Gold won map one, which lasted 53 minutes. On the second map they fought back to 10-10, but Gentle Mates closed it out 13-11 after 55 minutes. The decider on Summit ran for 57 minutes and finished 13-10 to Gentle Mates.

Coming through the upper bracket gives Gentle Mates a two-map ban advantage in the grand final. Shopify Rebellion Gold, led at the event by interim in-game leader alexis, drop into the lower bracket final against KRÜ Blaze.

This is Gentle Mates’ first appearance at the Championship. Their line-up of Marti, Nami, Wens, tokameite and berryx reached the upper final with 2-0 wins over Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. Their last three EMEA Stage 3 results before the event were wins over G2 Gozen and SK Nebula, both 2-1, and a 3-2 defeat to G2 Gozen.

The Elo power rankings already had Gentle Mates ahead. They sit fourth with a rating of 1844 and a 33-7 record from 40 rated matches. Shopify Rebellion Gold are sixth on 1809, with a 40-20 record from 60 rated matches.

Shopify Rebellion Gold had cleared SK Nebula and KRÜ Blaze without losing a map. Before travelling, they beat FlyQuest RED 3-1 and 2-1 and SwimTrek Blue 2-0 in North America Stage 2. At last year’s Championship in Seoul, Team Liquid Brazil beat them 3-2 in the title match.

The lower bracket final is a rematch. Shopify Rebellion Gold beat KRÜ Blaze in the upper semi-final. KRÜ then earned their place with lower bracket wins over Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC, both without dropping a map. MIBR GC finished fourth, which is worth $50,000. SK Nebula, one of three EMEA teams in São Paulo, placed joint fifth to sixth for $25,000. Their line-up included Scottish player fluxxy.

ON VA EN FINALE DES WORLDS ! pic.twitter.com/vAt2vVdyvY

— Gentle Mates (@gentlemates) October 30, 2026

Third place pays $70,000. The lower bracket final and the grand final are both best-of-five, after best-of-three series in the earlier rounds of the double-elimination bracket. Ten teams entered the event at Riot Games Arena, which Riot describes as the last Game Changers Championship to be held as a standalone event. In 2027 the Championship moves to Austin, Texas. For the first time it will run in the same city at the same time as VALORANT Champions, from 16 September to 10 October.

Shopify Rebellion Gold and KRÜ Blaze meet in the lower bracket final on Saturday 31 October at 15:00 BRT. The winner faces Gentle Mates GC in the grand final on Sunday 1 November at 15:00 BRT.

#4330. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

#4329. Vampire Survivors tier list - Ranking characters from base game and DLCs

Each DLC brought different characters and we have decided to rank each one and rank them on the Vampire Survivors tier list according to their late-game power.

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version: 1.16.111

Since the release of Vampire Survivors, people have been widely discussing things like "Who are the best characters in the game?" and other burning questions. There are, god knows, how many characters at the moment, but even then, this list can still expand with every update. Picking the most powerful character is essential to enjoying Vampire Survivors, and we are here to help with that.

Potent characters will mean an easier time, so if you're not looking for a challenge, they're the way to go. Also, feel free to check our Dead Cells weapons tier list as well as this tier list for Capybara Go.

About Queen Sigma Even though Queen Sigma can't pick up Golden Eggs like other heroes, she is still one of the most powerful characters, and it wouldn't be wrong to call her the best character without a doubt.

She uses the Victory Sword, which is one of the game’s most potent weapons. After levelling up, she gets +1% Might and +1% Growth, allowing her to become much more powerful. The main feature of Queen Sigma is her 333 max health, allowing her to survive longer.

About Red Death Red Death is the fastest and scariest hero in Vampire Survivors. The high speed makes this character suitable for finding Relic locations and fighting hidden bosses. Red Death uses the Death Spiral that can be easily combined with Axe in the same run. Its main feature is the 20% Might increase and the 100% Movement increase. These stats make Red Death one of the most potent heroes in Vampire Survivors.

Pungola is a mighty Vampire Survivors character that has two primary weapons: Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow. The hero gets +1% Might every level and can be unlocked by opening a special coffin in Mad Forest. Also, you should cast the spell “flymetothemoon” in Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane to unlock this hero.

Ambrojoe is an easily attainable hero that uses La Robba as a primary weapon. This character has average stats and no special abilities, making him the best option for beginners. We have to note that the weapon looks an awful lot like a Kinder Egg - we're actually not sure if it's an easter egg or not.

Dommario can be a good option for beginners due to his powerful defence and attack stats, but the main disadvantage of Dommario is speed. It is one of the slowest characters you can choose.

Megalo Menya Moonspell is overall the best character in Legacy of Moonspell DLC due to her combination of survivability and damage.

What stands out particularly is her invincibility, meaning she cannot take damage at all during certain periods. That said, this comes with a limitation; she will disappear when the current time limit expires. This makes her particularly powerful for clearing stages quickly.

Je-Ne-Viv is considered the most powerful character in Tides of the Foscari DLC, and that's why she's at the top of this part of our Vampire Survivors tier list. She has a unique weapon called Insatiable, which scales with Magnet and Greed stats, and comes with the Shadow Servant. Her abilities deal significant area-of-effect damage, making her a powerful character overall.

Crewmate Dino gains permanent stat boosts whenever any player's weapon reaches its max level. This ability makes him especially powerful in co-op mode, making him the best character in the Emergency Meeting DLC.

Megalo Impostor Rina has high base stats, special weapon mechanics, and the ability to scale through all phases of the game. Her toolkit is ideal for those who enjoy a playstyle that rewards aggressive tactics and strategic planning.

About Colonel Bahamut Colonel Bahamut stands out because of his great passive bonuses, like +100 Max Health and +50% Might. About Alucard Alucard is S-Tier and one of the best characters in the Ode to Castlevania DLC due to his high damage output, versatility, and healing abilities. His weapon mechanics allow for powerful area control, making him a top-tier choice for most runs.

Sonia Belmont is the other top-tier character in Ode to Castlevania. She has excellent scaling potential and powerful weapon synergies. Her ability to deal consistent dps while maintaining survivability is what makes her so good.

About Vlad Tepes Dracula Vlad Tepes Dracula has a deserving top position on this Vampire Survivors tier list since he is a character with high damage output and abilities that enhance survivability. His skills allow him to deal significant area damage, making him a standout choice for many players.

About Lisa Tepes Lisa Tepes provides excellent support with healing abilities and buffs that can sustain her and allies throughout runs. Her versatility and ability to boost stats make her invaluable in longer gameplay sessions. About Cornell Cornell has strong offensive capabilities with transformation mechanics that allow him to adapt to different combat scenarios effectively. And that’s our complete Vampire Survivors tier list. As you can see, the game has a significant diversity of exciting characters, and 3 of the best heroes in Vampire Survivors are Queen Sigma, Red Death, and Big Trouser. #4328. 8 Best Hallway Simulator JRPGs

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

To those unaware, the term “Hallway Sim” for JRPGs was derived from Final Fantasy 13, one of the black sheep of the series. It describes games where exploration takes a backseat to linear level design as you spend most of your time running down narrow corridors, fighting enemies, and watching the occasional cutscene before moving on to the next hallway.

And while that might sound like a recipe for disaster to anyone who enjoys getting lost in sprawling worlds, there’s something oddly comforting about a JRPG that knows exactly where it wants you to go. Of course, FF13 isn't the only game guilty of this design philosophy, nor is it necessarily the worst offender. Many JRPGs have traded sprawling overworlds for a more focused, linear experience, and some are all the better for it if you ask me.

If you love JRPGs but get bogged down by open world activities, check out the these JRPGs for players tired of open world.

So, if you're tired of open-world RPGs that seem to eat up every waking hour of your life, these hallway-simulator JRPGs might be exactly what you need, so why not set the term's derogatory meaning aside for just this once, pretty please?

We’re at the racelines, so I figured we’d open with the Tales of series, a line of games where I’ll gladly rise from my comatose grave to proudly defend Berseria. But see, you’re lucky because we’re talking about Tales of Arise today. What makes Arise stand out as a hallway simulator is how much it accomplishes with a largely linear structure.

The journey with Dahna’s rebellious gang of misfits is filled with a multitude of hub areas across various regions, and although they feature a bit of verticality here and there, the hallway bit quite literally shows up in the final act of the game, as hilarious as that may sound to someone who played it fully.

But hey, at least the real-time combat adds plenty of excitement to these otherwise straightforward maps and progression routes. The game is still an absolute blast to play, so don’t let anyone convince you otherwise, because Alphen and Shionne's budding growth certainly deserve your attention.

Despite its modern-day Tokyo setting, Tokyo Xanadu eX+ is a great example of a hallway simulator JRPG because its world is much more linear than its urban backdrop initially suggests. Don’t get me wrong, the game still has plenty to enjoy in its social-sim aspect that’ll strongly remind you of the Persona series' DNA.

But the cracks start to show once you dive into the actual gameplay, partly because the dungeons are (mostly) long corridors with small rooms in between, packed with enemies, your usual (and basic) environmental puzzles, and a boss waiting at the end. That doesn't make Tokyo Xanadu eX+ a bad JRPG, though, but I can see the repetition setting in for anyone else when the game railroads you along on this high-school high-jinks adventure.

Now, I know Soul Hackers 2 got a hefty amount of slack upon release and well past the honeymoon period, to the point where it had a divided audience, but hey, at least I’m in the minority who loved what I've played so far. However, I’d be lying to you if I didn’t admit that its actual world exploration feels surprisingly restrictive. All the way down to the dungeon design.

And the biggest offender is its Soul Matrix, where almost every character-specific dungeon is essentially a collection of long, repetitive corridors with branching paths that occasionally lead to treasure chests, enemies, or locked doors.

Even the main story dungeons aren't particularly special; if I’m being blunt, they often feel more like elaborate indoor mazes than places you'd genuinely want to explore, which is unfortunate because, aside from that, Soul Hackers 2 is a very decent JRPG if given the proper time and attention, with an adoring cast of characters at the helm.

Not every JRPG received the spotlight it deserved, as demonstrated by these obscure games from famous developers.

I’ll admit up front here: the Wild Arms series has a serious cult following. The first three games gave you these sprawling overworlds, goofy puzzle dungeons, and a Wild West-meets-fantasy vibe that nothing else quite matched. Then Wild Arms 4 came along and decided the best way to tell a story was to put you in a corridor… and keep you there.

Oh right, it does have one thing doing a bit of the heavy lifting: the hex-grid battle system. It’s a genuinely interesting twist on the combat system of other JRPGs at that time and keeps regular fights from feeling like standard menu-fests. But even that can’t fully hide how little there is to do between battles, since the game largely funnels you from one encounter to the next, with little opportunity to wander off the beaten path.

Scarlet Nexus has one of the coolest combat systems I’ve played in an action RPG; quite underrated if you ask me, but I have to be honest: you spend most of your time walking down corridors for the gameplay portion at least. And by the time you reach the endgame, it honestly feels like one long walk between fights every single time.

Don’t get me wrong; it’s a pretty good game, but it's built almost entirely out of hallways, and every main mission follows the same pattern. You push forward through a narrow, linear path, hit a small arena where a few Others drop in, and clear it out with your melee might and psychokinesis (PK).

The Brain Map and Bond Episodes add some welcome character progression and downtime, but they don't change the fact that Scarlet Nexus is a remarkably linear experience. But hey, as long as you try both of its two main characters’ routes, I promise Scarlet Nexus will be worth your time and investment, given how much dumb fun it offers.

I thought we’d dabble into the retro scene and talk about Grandia 2, one of the most beloved JRPGs on the Dreamcast. The combat is some of the best the genre has ever produced, and Ryudo is a genuinely fun protagonist, a grumpy mercenary who’d rather be anywhere else. But if you ask me what the game feels like from hour to hour, I’d say it’s like walking through a very pretty, very long hallway with a really good fight system attached.

Let’s talk about the dungeons because the game is built almost entirely out of narrow, winding paths that lead from Point A to Point B, with the occasional fork that gives you a treasure chest as a consolation prize for turning left. And to be fair, this is a very common JRPG design philosophy, especially from that era, since plenty of games from that generation are built around a story-first, linear structure.

In the most complimentary way I can put it, Grandia 2 is a hallway simulator with a killer combat system, a charming cast, and one of the most memorable villains of its time, but… just don’t go in expecting a world to explore.

I might be bending the rules here, but forgive me because I needed a way to compartmentalize this list without having one less entry. But hey, I guess that means this is a safe space to rave about Stranger of Paradise. Let’s get one thing straight, obviously. This is technically a loot-driven action RPG with a job system, which is about as JRPG as it gets, but the world barely exists, so there’s no cozy little town for you to wander, no overworld to explore, no little NPCs telling you about their lost cat or dad that ran out to get groceries.

Instead, you pick a mission from a menu, stare at a loading screen, and get tossed into a hallway-esque dungeon. Not that it’s a killing point, because this is, on all fronts, another fantastic Team Ninja game that gives you plenty of build options to take down its trash-fodder foes and hard-hitting boss fights. And if you’ve got the complete edition, the DLCs are a worthwhile plus for anyone who wants second helpings out of the game’s combat system.

As much as I’d want to make you roll your eyes by going with FF13, I decided the less obvious top pick to sign off with here would be Final Fantasy VII Remake. With Revelation coming in the first half of 2027, it just felt right.

The first part of this remake trilogy takes the opening few hours of the original, the bit in Midgar that you used to blow through in an afternoon, and turns it into a full-length game. That’s an ambitious swing, but despite what some of the divided fanbase may tell you, it works splendidly to give its charming cast of characters a whole new sense of direction and relationship-building moments.

What's particularly noticeable is the contrast between Midgar's enormous scale and how little of it you're actually allowed to explore. Even when the game introduces side quests and optional activities in areas like the Sector 7 Slums or Wall Market, these locations are relatively small hubs connected by straightforward routes, not fully explorable districts.

It’s not a true hallway-sim JRPG, as the term suggests for its sister game in the series, but these corridor-esque maps leave little room for meaningful exploration or player-driven detours. Again, not a diss at the game since it’s a lovely time for both hardcore fans and newcomers.

If you're lacking in time or energy for long games, try one of these JRPGs for Players Tired of 100-Hour Time Commitments.

Share your take with fellow players. Keep it constructive, relevant, and respectful.

#4327. Tenebris Somnia Review – A Hair-Raising And Entertaining Throwback

Tenebris Somnia channels the old-school appeal of classic point-and-click adventures, survival horror, and full-motion-video (FMV) experiences, then smartly modernizes them to create a creepy, entertaining experience. Surviving the twisted threats of a demonic dream world is a tightly packed adventure that rewards you with what’s essentially an impressive indie horror film peppered throughout. It’s a nightmare you may not want to wake up from.

The blend of live-action and in-game storytelling works well in Tenebris Somina’s adventure, which begins when protagonist Julia visits the apartment of her filmmaker ex-boyfriend, Ivan, after suffering recurring nightmares of him being massacred by monsters. What begins as a well-meaning check-in on his status spirals down an unsettling rabbit hole when Julia’s worst fears are realized and then some. The dialogue-free tale presents a scary but fascinating exploration of obsession, both in art and in romance, that constantly delivers surprising, and at times upsetting, revelations during its eight-hour runtime. While Tenebris Somnia sometimes leans a little too far into “tell, don’t show” territory when explaining the cool lore of its supernatural threats, I never felt lost or confused about the wild things that regularly unfold on screen.

FMV experiences are nothing new, but Tenebris Somnia’s live-action scenes are a highlight. They’re well shot, sport impressively gruesome practical effects, and even present visual clues that make them important to gameplay. These scenes are additive, never taking too much time away from the in-game action, and they feel well placed to elicit the strongest emotional response. I also appreciate how the live scenes fit thematically, as much of Tenebris Somnia’s tale centers on a horror film shot by Ivan and Julia that significantly impacted their former relationship; at times, it’s like watching a movie about the movie. While I enjoy smaller moments, like opening a door to trigger a live-action jump scare, the filmmaking succeeds in selling Julia's emotions and the cast's reactions. Seeing real fear, concern, and determination in Julia’s eyes as she navigates a dreamworld made up of Ivan’s memories helped endear me to what would otherwise be a featureless pixel sprite.

Gameplay may look unimpressive due to its old-school adventure game presentation, but Tenebris Somnia’s spin on familiar survival-horror mechanics hits the right notes. Taking place entirely within a dreamlike version of a four-story apartment building, you’ll traverse floors collecting and combining objects and deciphering clues to solve well-crafted puzzles. I’m impressed by how well the game’s puzzles make the most of its limited graphical presentation, including clever scenarios involving mirror/screen reflections I won’t spoil, and how consistently creative they are. One devious exercise even utilizes the game’s limited save points as an unexpected resource in a way that changes how you approach your adventure going forward. No matter how strange puzzles become, they are never opaque, requiring just enough out-of-the-box thinking to make me feel smart when I connect the dots.

Battling grotesque monsters (which, naturally, look even creepier in live-action) also feels good, with melee and gunplay sporting deliberate animations reminiscent of classic adventure games without feeling mechanically clunky. Taking on multiple enemies by swinging a pipe or blowing them away with a shotgun feels better than it looks, and the most intense encounters end just as they approach the line of becoming overwhelming.

Boss battles, perhaps most unexpectedly for a largely puzzle-focused adventure, are fun and distinct from each other, be it wave-based bouts against small gremlin-like foes, protecting a fragile effigy of yourself from a parade of demented house servants, or battling literal mirror images of a tentacled flesh monster the Resident Evil series would be proud to claim. Managing limited ammo and health strikes a good balance of feeling tense but not oppressive. Playing conservatively is rewarding, as few non-boss threats need to be engaged if you can evade them well enough. But when I did find myself down to my last bullet or on the verge of death, Tenebris Somnia lets you feel the pinch just long enough before dropping a box of bullets or a health vial at the right moment.

Tenebris Somnia mines the enjoyable nostalgia of playing the horror games of yesteryear without feeling dated in the worst way. Weaving a solid indie horror film adds to the experience rather than feeling like a gimmick. The result is a captivating, well-executed survival-horror romp that maintains a hair-raising atmosphere with a fraction of the pixels of other genre giants.

#4325. KRÜ Blaze recover from opening map loss to beat Shopify Rebellion Gold and reach final

KRÜ Blaze dropped the first map and then took the next three on Saturday 31 October. The win reverses their upper bracket semi-final defeat to Shopify Rebellion Gold and sends the Argentine-based side into the final of the VCT Game Changers Championship 2026. Shopify Rebellion Gold’s campaign ends with the loss.

The result also cuts against the power rankings. Shopify Rebellion Gold arrived as the 10th-ranked team with a rating of 1782. KRÜ Blaze sit 20th on 1742, although their 63-21 record across 84 rated matches is the stronger of the two.

Shopify Rebellion Gold struck first, taking a 47-minute opening map. KRÜ Blaze levelled on the quickest map of the series, which lasted 37 minutes, and edged ahead with a 50-minute third.

The fourth map was by some distance the longest of the night at 70 minutes. KRÜ Blaze closed it out to settle the best-of-five without needing a decider.

The meeting on 27 October had been far more one-sided. Shopify Rebellion Gold won that upper bracket semi-final 2-0, which pushed KRÜ Blaze into the lower half of the draw. Before that, KRÜ Blaze had opened their playoff run by beating Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper bracket quarter-finals.

Saturday’s victory was KRÜ Blaze’s third successive series win in the lower bracket. Both earlier wins were sweeps. They beat Team Liquid Brazil 2-0 in the quarter-finals, then dispatched MIBR GC by the same score in the semi-finals.

That run means they have won seven of the eight maps played since dropping out of the upper bracket. They also came into the event as winners of the Latin America regional final, where they beat Akave Esports Black 3-1.

#4324. Pokémon Masters EX tier list - The best sync pairs to use

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version:  2.74.0 - Latest Additions:  Arc Suit Hau & Raichu, Arc Suit Gladion & Silvally, Maxie (Fall 2026) & Ting-Lu

With over 200 collectable Sync Pairs of Pokémon and their masters, it sure can get confusing for new players and veterans alike to come to a definitive conclusion about which ones are the best and which ones they should avoid. Pokémon Masters EX, the officially licensed game by DeNA, has brought tons of new Sync Pairs for players to collect and use with their fifth anniversary. This Pokémon Masters EX tier list is here to serve as a curated list of Sync Pairs that can help you in your journey of becoming the best Pokémon trainer.

You will find all the answers in this tier list as to whether a certain Sync Pair is better or worse than another. Keep in mind that tier lists are inherently subjective in nature. Use your own judgment while investing your resources in these Sync Pairs, but feel free to take inspiration from them.

Stay tuned for the updated versions of this tier list - we will make sure to add new Sync Pairs as they are released while also adjusting the individual categories based on future balance adjustments.

Let’s get you right to our Pokémon Masters EX tier list!

The main focus of judging Sync Pairs in this tier list will be mostly on their damage-dealing capabilities. Most of the Sync Pairs here have striking abilities that help them deal more damage. Of course, some exceptions exist, like the Steven & Deoxys (Attack Forme) Sync Pair that can also boost the critical hit rate of all allies. However, that's just an added bonus to their already high damage multipliers and potential value.

Some of the most notable damage dealers are going to be Red & Pikachu, Lucas & Dialga, and Steven & Deoxys (Attack Forme). Red & Pikachu's special move B Thunderbolt is a massive hyper-scaling damaging move that increases its own damage the more it is used. Such moves are not only good in PvE content where fights can drag out, but also in certain PvP situations against tanky stall team comps. Lucas & Dialga is possibly the best Dragon-type Sync Pair available due to their special move Dragon Zone that can boost the stats of all Dragon-types. Steven & Deoxys (Attack Forme) is the ultimate counter to Sync Pairs that reduce the stats of enemies. Their passive ability, Downside Up, states that whenever an enemy reduces the stats of Steven and Deoxys (Attack Forme), the move instead increases their stats by the same amount. #4323. A Mass Effect 5 Trailer Featuring Liara Appears To Have Leaked Following BioWare's Closure

In case you missed the tragic news yesterday, EA laid off 400 employees this week, including all of BioWare. The studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more, has been shut down, and its last remaining project was canceled. The game in question was a fifth entry in the Mass Effect universe, and BioWare shared very little about it – not even an official name. Following the studio's closure, however, a trailer for the sci-fi sequel started circulating around the internet.

While no official BioWare representatives have confirmed that the footage is real, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier claims that it is. Schreier has a history of credible reporting in the field, and was the first to break the news about the layoffs. IGN has also stated that it confirmed the trailer's legitimacy.

If you want to see for yourself, you can watch the trailer on Reddit.

"The following is in-engine footage form our small team," text at the start of the video reads. "It uses our pre-production assets." The footage shows no gameplay, but includes a good-looking CG cutscene of a new protagonist speaking with an asari woman in a crowded bar. As he tells her about his life, we see glimpses of him as a soldier, then as some kind of spy, traveling to several planets to track down conflicts and "stopping them before they start." After the asari woman reveals that she's been "starting the fires" he's trying to prevent, another woman behind her lowers a hood. This new woman reveals herself as Liara T'Soni, one of Mass Effect's most iconic characters.

Then, Liara and the protagonist team up to take out the woman at the bar and her henchmen, using guns and telekinetic abilities. The trailer fades to black, then fades back in to reveal the game's would-be title: Mass Effect Universe. It's a great-looking trailer – it's a shame the game will never see the light of day.

If you want to join us in grieving BioWare, we republished an oral history of the studio that was originally written by former editor Matt Bertz in 2016. You can also read our cover stories on BioWare's most recent releases: Dragon Age: The Veilguard, Mass Effect: Legendary Edition, Anthem, and Mass Effect Andromeda.

#4322. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4321. Dead Cells weapons tier list - every weapon ranked

Not sure which melee weapon, ranged weapon, grenade, turret, or trap to bring? We've got you covered.

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version 3.5.15

Dead Cells has a lot of weapons, making it perfect for a tier list ranking every weapon. Throughout the game, you'll come across melee weapons, ranged weapons, traps, turrets, and even grenades, each with different effects like damage over time or freezing an enemy in their place. It can feel a little overwhelming, even though they're often slow or difficult to unlock and discover.

That's where our Dead Cells weapons tier list comes in. While we haven't gone into detail about most of the weapons here, we wanted to give you a quick overview of the best, the brightest, and, of course, most destructive tools in your arsenal to help you survive this perilous world.

Which weapons should you unlock in Dead Cells? It's a tough question, isn't it? You only have limited cells to spend on unlocking blueprints, so picking the best weapons to unlock can be tricky and overwhelming. We recommend starting with our S-tier weapons and working your way down from there. Most are ranked by their base damage numbers, but where a weapon or skill does something special and interesting, we've made sure to note it.

Of course, ultimately, it all comes down to personal preference. Make sure you read every weapon's description and decide if it would suit you. Some weapons have extra effects like applying a damage-over-time effect, like Bleed, or even combining with other weapons to create a one-two punch kind of effect. It's all personal. Dead Cells weapons tier list So, without further ado, let's get down to business. We've taken the time to break everything down by type for you: melee weapons, ranged weapons, shields (yes, they count), turrets and traps, and grenades. Each has its place in battle. Each will help you in some way to reach the end of the road.

If you disagree with anything on this list, then please let us know in the comments! These are a matter of opinion, after all, aside from their ranking on base damage. Critical damage is also important, so be sure to read the weapon description to take that into account.

Melee weapons make up the bread and butter of your arsenal, comprising everything from swords and axes to a spiked wrecking ball and a giant shark. Yes, a shark. Here, we've gone through and listed every melee weapon, ranked according to base damage.

Some weapons stand out more than others, of course. The Ferryman's Lantern allows you to kill an enemy to gather its soul. Then, as a secondary attack, charge it to fire those souls as projectiles, dealing critical hits if three souls are shot at the same time. With a base damage of 164 plus secondary damage of 107, then critical hits applying 429 damage, this is a monster of a weapon.

Others stand out for their usefulness and fun factor. With the Maw of the Deep, your third attack throws the shark, rooting the enemy and inflicting bleed. Rooted targets will then take critical damage - 158 base, and 270 critical.

The Rapier allows you to critical hit immediately after a roll or parry, and if you play the game like us, you'll be rolling around a lot anyway. With the Meat Skewer, your first attack places you behind the enemy, with your second hit applying critical damage. The Pure Nail comes courtesy of fellow Metroidvania Hollow Knight, allowing you to attack while moving left, right, and up. Drop down on an enemy and attack downwards to "bounce," just like in Hollow Knight, applying damage while in the air.

Finally, the Hard Light Sword is actually two weapons in one, along with the Hard Light Gun. A reference to the acclaimed Hyper Light Drifter, these weapons work in tandem. Fire the Hard Light Gun into enemies to damage and mark them. Then, the Hard Light Sword deals critical damage based on the number of shots it has received. Sword hits also recharge ammo for the gun, which (unlike other ranged weapons, more on those next) doesn't recharge over time. It's an elegant dance that might not be the most powerful, but is undoubtedly one of the most fun tools in the Dead Cells weapons arsenal.

Time for the first of our tier lists, then! Here we go: Rank Weapon S Ferryman's Lantern, Cursed Sword, War Spear, Tombstone, Flint, Oven Axe, Wrecking Ball, Giantkiller, Vampire Killer, Bible, Alucard's Sword, Death's Scythe, Misericorde A Toothpick, Symmetrical Lance, Shrapnel Axes, Hattori's Katana, Meat Skewer, Broadsword, Impaler, Crowbar, Twin Daggers, Hayabusa Boots, Vorpan, Shovel, Maw of the Deep, Rapier, Baseball Bat, Nutcracker, Pure Nail, Morning Star, Whip Sword, Sewing Scissors B Balanced Blade, Flashing Fans, Spite Sword, Rusty Sword, Bone, Swift Sword, Frantic Sword, Iron Staff, Assassin's Dagger, Rhythm n' Bouzouki, Seismic Strike, Wrenching Whip, Oiled Sword, Hayabusa Gauntlets, Blood Sword, Panchaku, Gold Digger, Machete and Pistol, Hard Light Sword, Giant Comb C Flawless, Sadist's Stiletto, Valmont's Whip, Torch, Abyssal Trident, Hand Hook, Spiked Boots, Bladed Tonfas, Dagger of Profit, Snake Fangs, Scythe Claw, Tentacle, King Scepter, Queen's Rapier, Starfury, Spartan Sandals

Ranged weapons are extremely helpful in Dead Cells, especially when you don't want to get close to an enemy. Most use ammunition that regenerates over time, or can be retrieved from enemies on death or following a successful parry, in the case of arrows. Some, like the combined Hard Light Sword and Gun mentioned on the previous page, have a special function - in this case, ammo doesn't recharge passively and instead must be recharged by landing hits with the Hard Light Sword.

Here's how we ranked the Dead Cells tier list for ranged weapons. Rank Weapon S Money Shooter, Ice Crossbow, Throwable Objects, Heavy Crossbow, Multiple-nocks Bow, Sonic Carbine, Barrel Launcher, Fire Blast, Magic Missiles, Medusa's Head, Anathema, Laser Glaive A Chakram of the Queen, The Boy's Axe, Peril Glyphs, Boomerang, Explosive Crossbow, Bow and Endless Quiver, Repeater Crossbow, Quick Bow, Laser Glaive, Gilded Yumi, Blowgun, Marksman's Bow, Ice Shards, Cross, Throwing Axe B Electric Whip, Lightning Bolt, War Javelin, Pyrotechnics, Nerves of Steel, Infantry Bow, Killing Deck, Hemorrhage C Beginner's Bow, Frost Blast, Ice Bow Firebrands, Hokuto's Bow, Magic Bow, Throwing Knife, Alchemic Carbine

Shields might be a boring choice for your adventure through Dead Cells, but don't sleep on them. Hold down a shield's assigned button to hold it up after 0.37 seconds. Attacks that hit the front are reduced by the shield's damage absorption percentage, typically around 75%, while also dealing damage to the enemy by the damage number listed on the shield.

Shields can also be used to parry attacks. Tap the button rather than hold it down, and it attempts a parry. If no attack hits during that window, you can't block or parry again for a little under a second. If your parry is successful, then a few things can happen: you can parry or block again immediately and enjoy an additional effect, depending on the attack.

Carrying a shield also passively creates a force field for 0.5 seconds after you take damage, absorbing most damage except DoT effects like poison and some enemy attacks.

Here, we've ranked shields in Dead Cells by their base block damage, meaning the damage the enemy takes after you block an attack. As always, read the shield's in-game description for any interesting effects, like AoE damage. Rank Weapon S Spiked Shield, Greed Shield, Punishment, Knockback Shield, Alucard's Shield A Force Shield, Thunder Shield, Assault Shield, Front Line Shield, Ice Shield B Rampart, Bloodthirsty Shield C Old Wooden Shield, Cudgel, Parry Shield

Deployable skills in Dead Cells come in three forms: traps and turrets, grenades, and various miscellaneous powers. It isn't possible to start with these skills without the Recycling Tubes upgrade.

First, let's cover deployable skills like traps and turrets. These come in powered and unpowered forms. Powered skills, such as turrets, need you to remain within their proximity for them to function. Line of sight is best, with the effective radius decreased if blocked by terrain. As long as you're within proximity, though, you'll notice a line of electricity connecting you to the deployed skill, allowing it to function.

Unpowered deployable skills are typically traps that don't actively attack on your behalf, such as traps that activate when the enemy steps onto them.

Let's rank the various types of deployable skills. First up, turrets. The Sinew Slicer is particularly worth noting. You'll come across it early, and it makes short work of early enemies without placing you in danger. Rank Skill S Barnacle, Scavenged Bombard, Heavy Turret, Cleaver A Double Crossb-o-matic, Sinew Slicer B Tesla Coil C Flamethrower Turret

Next up, traps and miscellaneous powers. The Emergency Door skill simply spawns a door in front of you, which acts like a regular door, meaning it can be destroyed to stun enemies on the other side. The Night Light is extremely situational and can be deployed in the Forgotten Sepulcher to help with the Darkness. Requiring 120 seconds to recharge, it can be thrown to a location to create a temporary light at that location. Touch it to replenish your light aura. Rank Skill S Crusher A Explosive Decoy B Wolf Trap C Night Light, Emergency Door

Grenades in Dead Cells do exactly what you expect: they explode. What more could you want? Simply throw, and enjoy! Some have added effects, of course, and can be paired with other skills or weapons for greater use. The Ice Grenade freezes enemies, for example, and the Root Grenade roots enemies, causing damage over time and keeping them rooted. The Magnetic Grenade is useful in crowded rooms. After a few moments, it attracts enemies in a large area, then explodes to deal electrical damage over time.

Grenades, like other skills, aren't exactly consumables as you would expect in other games. Rather they each have a set cooldown, meaning they can be reused over and over again.

The Hunter's Grenade is situational, which is why it's ranked C, but it's quite useful at the same time. Throw it to "annoy" a monster. When its health drops to 40% or less, use "Blueprint Extractor" to grab a blueprint. Rank Skill S Powerful Grenade, Holy Water A Infantry Grenade, Cluster Grenade, Magnetic Grenade B Stun Grenade, Ice Grenade, Fire Grenade, Root Grenade, Oil Grenade, Swarm C Hunter's Grenade

#4320. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

#4319. Wuthering Waves and the Constant Pursuit of Improving the Player Experience

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

This article was produced in collaboration with our sponsor, Kuro Games.

Live service games rely on two major factors to stay afloat: constant content and community satisfaction. These aims sound perfectly aligned. After all, players want more things to do in their favorite games, so just giving them more should do it all, right? Easier said than done, especially when improper quality control can doom a game rapidly, especially in the eyes of new players.

Leaking in a similar vein to Persona 3 Reload, footage showcasing a Persona 1 Remake has appeared, looking almost too good to be true.

This Article was made with help from our sponsor, Kuro Games. Wuthering Waves is a game that teetered on that brink, fumbling its first impression with early execution that left much to be desired across various levels, prompting a period of deep reflection and iteration. Despite this slow start, I'd put WuWa right alongside No Man's Sky on the pedestal of "Most Improved Games from Launch", largely thanks to Kuro Games' willingness to respond to community grievances with actual, tangible change.

From gameplay overhauls, massively improved visual presentation, to a heavily expanded story that feels like it's just now hitting a second wind, Wuthering Waves is a refreshing example of just how far a team with open communication and pure passion can push a product toward excellence, allowing WuWa to stand alongside titans in their genre’s sphere.

As we approach 3.8, it's really wild to look back on just how rough WuWa's initial launch was, rife with complaints about an overall experience that still needed polish. Yet, its remarkable combat already displayed the clear potential of a standout game, and Kuro was quick to show just how much things were willing to change.

As early as 1.3, the plot was starting to roll, giving early adopters a real incentive to keep coming back with each update, even as bugs were constantly being ironed out. Kuro has been great about acknowledging and squashing these bugs.

Even this early, you can see how Kuro was improving not only the gameplay feel, but the character presentation. 1.0 WuWa still had room for growth in character writing, a flaw that has been so rewarding to see them improve on patch after patch. This progress is another grand showcase of Kuro's resilience and unwavering commitment to quality.

Despite this willingness to shake things up, WuWa never forsook the genuinely interesting parts of its world that caught the community's attention all those years ago. Instead, Kuro built on to what worked, shown in 2.0's sweeping set of improvements.

2.0 felt like WuWa's Realm Reborn moment, combining all the early community critiques of the presentation, exploration, and story into a proper grand reintroduction. With new features like flight, old pain points when it came to grinding and map clearing were easy to handle, all while feeling like a proper reward.

After the departures of various leading developers, PlatinumGames wants fans of Bayonetta to know they aren't through with the Umbra Witch.

While other open-world games generally have players explore their maps on foot, WuWa is constantly improving the exploration experience with new vehicles, methods of traversal, and tricks to keep the world exciting. Solaris-3 always feels like it's getting bigger, reminding players that WuWa is a proper sci-fi setting, with this distinctive blend of sci-fi identity and exploration being one of the reasons it continues to draw me in.

The Wuthering Waves community itself is more than willing to chirp up about issues. Kuro Games, in turn, respects and takes player feedback seriously, maintaining an open and proactive dialogue with the community.

Despite this slow start, I'd put WuWa right alongside No Man's Sky on the pedestal of "Most Improved Games from Launch", largely thanks to Kuro Games' willingness to respond to community grievances with actual, tangible change.

The studio isn't without fault, as the game's rough launch showed, but Kuro makes it easy to sit in their corner when they're so willing to fuse their vision for the game with the community's genuine grievances. The game's longest-running pain point, its lack of early character implementation, is already on the way out. Fan-favorite characters such as Aemeath shows just how far the team has come, with both its storytelling and character writing now reaching an exceptionally high standard. We might be seeing an all-time story for new players post 4.0.

WuWa has more than lived up to my top expectation for games in the genre: a strong protagonist. Watching a MC actually improve and change over the course of the story is so nice to properly see, and Rover's journey from 1.0 to now is genuinely some of the best in the genre.

If you like Action RPGs and other similar titles have burnt you by stonewalling devs or flatlining content, Wuthering Waves is the best recommendation I can possibly give. Constant, open communication, a real active fanbase, and a game created with mountains of love, WuWa really is the full package.

If you're a new or returning player, make sure to check out the official Wuthering Waves page for updates, dev blogs, and upcoming news for the game as a whole. Major title updates are the best time to join, and the current story arc is entering its climactic finale, so don't wait!

#4318. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Review - Silver Bullet

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives at a crossroads for the series, thanks in large part to the inconsistent quality of recent entries. With a shaky predecessor, Infinity Ward had a lot to repair and conclude, especially with 4 set to bookend the rebooted Modern Warfare series. Fortunately, backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 makes up for the past and then some.

Modern Warfare 4 continues after the events of 2023’s Modern Warfare 3, with Captain Price hellbent on stopping Makarov and his higher-ups. The story features shifting perspectives, from a new group of ragtag Korean soldiers to familiar characters like Gaz. The character dynamics harken back to the original trilogy, especially in the boots-on-the-ground missions with the South Korean unit, led by Park (played by Beef actor Young Mazino).

For a series that, at least recently, has been more spectacle than story, giving the stakes the time they deserve is nice. While it moves away from the stealthy and modernized elements, it makes sense for the matters at hand. The majority of Modern Warfare 4’s attempts at wrapping up the overarching plot of the rebooted series works, but it rushes through some character arcs and story beats in uneven fashion. Furthermore, much of the game’s cast, especially Mads Mikkelson’s Archer and Prisca Kim’s Ri Ju-Young, are underutilized, which is a shame since they both deliver great performances.

Despite the shortcomings of the campaign, Call of Duty's bread and butter, multiplayer, still delivers. While it doesn’t have the fluidity of Black Ops’ newer entries, the customization and design of weapons and maps make it worth digging into. From small, intimate shooting galleries with Mumbai and Nautical to wide free-for-alls like Coal and Reactor U92, the range helps maintain excitement, even if it gets repetitive over time.

The variety of multiplayer modes keeps things fresh on the battlefield. Returning modes like standard Team Deathmatch and Kill Confirmed continue that enjoyable competitive flair that made them the stars that they are. However, new modes like Combat Outpost and Hijack fit right into the already great lineup. In particular, Combat Outpost upscales your typical 6v6 player count to 24v24, leading to more action and teamwork. Hanging onto a team’s tank, shooting enemies from afar, and taking back outposts is exhilarating, even if it can all go bad moments later by a well-placed RPG shot.

Even after hours of gameplay, the variety of options to craft your perfect gun is impressive. Figuring out the best scope, ammo, stock, and muzzle, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them, is a fun way of customizing your playstyle. Gunny, a mechanic that helps optimize your gun for certain styles, can help with decision paralysis, but I rarely used it. Not many FPSs go that far and Modern Warfare 4’s commitment to the feature makes it stand out.

The newest mode, DMZ, impresses out of the gate. After a few flat attempts in the past, this is the definitive Call of Duty extraction shooter, whether you play solo, or in duos or trios. Immediately, you’re thrust into the wide open world of Hajin and left to fend for yourselves with what you have and what you can gather and extract. Fans of Arc Raiders and Marathon should feel right at home as the gameplay borrows from the typical extraction shooter experience. Intense, action-packed moments keep you coming back after every win or loss. And the excellent gunplay and level design elevate it into something worthwhile, no matter how you play.

Despite not encountering many live players during my time in Hajin in DMZ, it still proves challenging, even for seasoned pros. The world is not your friend, and taking risks can come at a high cost. A good team, as well as a thoughtful loadout and traits, are required to survive. The unpredictability of it all keeps you on your toes, making for an exciting addition to the already strong multiplayer suite.

Regardless of the mode, Modern Warfare 4 is one of the best-looking Call of Duty titles to date. New York and Paris are lifelike, and it truly embodies the realistic, modern aesthetic the series has always aimed to achieve. However, I encountered a few technical hiccups, especially in the campaign. Slow framerate plagues some high-octane scenes and texture loading is frequent across the board. These distractions are far from game-breaking, but enough to be noticeable.

While the plot execution is a bit shaky, engaging multiplayer options, including DMZ, aptly demonstrate that Infinity Ward can still deliver compelling military-FPS experiences. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a strong return to form that serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries.

#4317. Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

There's a new Arc Raiders patch that's fairly small, but one with fixes everyone is going to appreciate.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

Neither TYLOO nor Lynn Vision is expected to play again before the cutoff. That leaves the Asian race effectively over.

The Lisbon event was a Valve Tier 2 tournament run by Hyped and PEW PEW. It ran from 29 October to 1 November with 13 teams and a prize pool of €12,187.50. Groups were GSL-format best-of-threes, followed by single-elimination best-of-three playoffs. TYLOO are listed in joint fifth to eighth place.

IEM Beijing is a far bigger draw on paper. ESL is staging it from 2 to 8 November at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena. It is S-Tier and Valve Tier 1, with 16 teams playing for $1,250,000.

TYLOO were not alone in stepping away from Lisbon. Natus Vincere also withdrew, and the organisers cited the same Beijing commitment for both teams. For NAVI, the withdrawal leaves their Major chances unchanged. They had until 19 October to pull out, but were still registered after that deadline. EA shut down legendary RPG developer BioWare this week, canceling its in-development fifth Mass Effect game as a result. Despite the closure, Amazon Prime’s upcoming Mass Effect streaming series will proceed as planned, according to a report by IGN.

Amazon MGM Studios began developing a Mass Effect series in 2024. At the time, Mass Effect series executive producer Mike Gamble confirmed the show isn't a retelling of the video games, saying, “The show will explore a brand-new story within the universe's timeline, and will be set after the original trilogy. This includes showrunners Doug Jung (The Cloverfield Paradox, Star Trek Beyond) and Daniel Casey (F9: The Fast Saga, Wardriver), former Marvel Studios head Avi Arad, and Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik. #4312. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4310. Nearly 3 in 4 Gamers Are More Likely to Wait for Sales, Newzoo and G2A Find

A Montreal-based Game enthusiast who has been writing about the industry since 2013.

Price and gaming has taken on an entirely new meaning over the last year. The idea of waiting for a sale became a borderline meme over a decade ago, when Steam started running infamous deep-discount sales on digital games. A cursory search for “Gabe” or “Steam Sale” can be a long timetraveling road through years of in-jokes from the enthusiast community. These goofs and gags barely hold up all these years later, but they do harken back to a simpler time in the world of games pricing.

Today, conversations around discounts, sales, and pricing will launch just about anyone from the wide-world of gaming into a tirade about a whole host of criticism of the game industry: what do we do about physical games, do we even own digital games, is Mario Kart World worth X number of dollars. The list goes on. In the market of 2026, between the cost of individual games, the increasing price of hardware, live-service games, and monthly subscriptions, there are more factors than ever that influence player spending habits. It’s a fascinating time to look into how pricing dynamics are influencing the industry.

A report from Newzoo and G2A.COM found that 73% of surveyed players say they are more likely to wait for sales these days. The survey included 6,166 active PC or console players aged 18–55 across six countries, all of whom had purchased or played at least one AAA or AA game in the previous year. The study, “Game purchasing behavior in an era of choice” investigates how modern PC and console players are choosing to spend their hard-earned money in 2026. And while, yes, most players are happy to let the release date come and go so they can get a good deal on a given game, that doesn’t mean that players are entirely content to wait particularly long for a discount.

Wardogs lead developer Joe Brammer took to X (formerly Twitter) to offer another perspective on why studios are struggling to stay afloat.

Looking back at their purchases over the past three years, respondents reported buying just 42% of games before or during release month: 17% through pre-orders and 25% during the month itself. So how does this break down outside of the launch window?

In summary, of the purchases respondents recalled making over the past three years, 82% happened before release or within a game’s first year, including pre-orders. The remaining 18% happened more than a year after release. Crucially, it’s worth bearing in mind that this describes the timing of reported purchases. Still, it highlights how important it is for publishers keep a game top-of-mind after launch, and make sure players are able to take advantage of discounts and other offers post-launch.

Among players who buy beyond release month, the average expected wait for a discount worth considering is 4.9 months. And naturally, how deep the discount cuts plays a big role in purchasing behaviour.

On average, respondents consider a game reasonably priced at 29% off, and Newzoo notes that a 45% discount represents a ‘good deal.’ In their sample, audiences considered a 70% cut a potential red flag to a game’s quality, which is an interesting note that’s hard to unsee when you browse Steam.

Now's your chance to save 50% on one of the best releases of the summer.

One of the other notable data points from the study is that despite players being happy to wait for discounts, they also consider games a very high-value medium. In fact, 69% consider it better value than entertainment such as television, films and music, while 62% agree that game prices reflect rising development costs and complexity. Of course, that doesn’t mean audiences aren’t always still looking for a deal if they can take advantage of one.

“With nearly 60% of purchases occurring later than release month, publishers need long-term monetisation strategies that go well beyond the first week or month,” Newzoo research director Alexis Pamboris said in the press release.

Where people shop is another piece of the puzzle. Official digital storefronts (PSN, Steam, etc.) are expectedly dominant, but 24% of subjects in the study claim to use third-party marketplaces to purchase or research a title. G2A, which co-authored the report and runs its own marketplace, states that the alternate purchasing channels give players more choice. As stated by G2A chief business officer Katarzyna Jakubiec, “different purchasing channels serve different consumer needs.”

Most players, especially those with a Steam backlog, can probably relate to some of Newzoo and G2A’s findings. Waiting for a sale is a familiar part of deciding what to buy, from a box of cereal to a piping-hot copy of Grand Theft Auto VI. What’s interesting is how clearly that patience shows up in the numbers. Players still want new games, but many are willing to let release day pass until the price feels right. For publishers, the challenge is giving them a reason to finally move something from the wishlist to the library.

For a full deep-dive on all that findings inside Newzoo and G2A's report, you can visit their site here.
